chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon to the people in Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage in the Mosque of Al-Khayf. He praised God and extolled Him, then said: 'May God assist a servant who hears my words, retains them, and conveys them to those who have not heard them. There are many bearers of understanding who are not themselves scholars, and many bearers of understanding who convey it to those more knowledgeable than themselves. There are three things in which the heart of a Muslim does not deceive him: sincerity of action for God, giving counsel to the leaders of the Muslims, and adhering to their community. For their call surrounds them from behind. Muslims are brothers; their blood is equal, and the lowest among them strives to fulfill the pledge of the highest. And they are a single hand against whoever is other than them.'

key_terms.تَتَكَافَأُ دِمَاؤُهُمْ: Their blood is equal (equal in value)

ai.seo_question: What are the three things that do not deceive a Muslim's heart according to the Prophet's sermon in Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal underscores the critical role of *taqlid* and knowledge transmission in Shia tradition, distinguishing between mere carriers of information (*hamil al-fiqh*) and true jurists, a concept vital for understanding the development of the scholarly hierarchy. It links the preservation of faith through accurate transmission to the political and spiritual unity of the community under the Imams, emphasizing that loyalty to the *Imama* and communal solidarity are inseparable from sincere devotion to God. The emphasis on 'three things' reflects a structured approach to maintaining doctrinal purity and social cohesion during the Farewell Pilgrimage, a pivotal moment in Islamic history.
